prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer is seated looking down at their own towel-covered lap (about 0.4–0.6 m below) and an elevated leg/footrest structure (0.3–0.5 m away) with a round UV nail lamp on top, while a supply caddy on the left sits lower at roughly 0.6–0.8 m and the floor is darkest at 1.0–1.2 m below. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer turns slightly rightward as a second person seated to the upper right (0.5–0.8 m away, facing toward the camera wearer's lap with their head and upper torso out of view above the frame) rests their right hand on top of the bright white nail lamp (0.3–0.4 m from the camera) in frames 3–5, and the camera wearer's own two hands rise from the lower left and bottom edge (0.5–0.7 m) in frames 1–3 to approach and touch the other person's fingers at 0.3–0.4 m in frames 4–5. Everything visible—the supply caddy on the left, the handheld control on the lap, the lamp, and the other person's outstretched hand—is within arm's reach of both people and separated by less than 0.5 m. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height tiers between the raised hands and lamp in the foreground, the lap at mid-depth, and the recessed tray and floor below, including the overlapping depth layers when the camera wearer's hands reach over the lamp in frames 4 and 5. However, the depth map is unreliable on bright white surfaces in frames 1 and 2, where the white lamp and cushioned leg rest saturate to nearly uniform maximum brightness, making their relative distances indistinguishable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map outlines the spatial footprints of the two people in the scene—the camera wearer occupying the lower-left and central lap area (0.4–0.7 m away) and the second person occupying the upper-right region (0.5–0.8 m away, facing toward the centre with their head and torso cropped out of frame)—alongside the rounded nail lamp on the elevated rest (0.3–0.5 m away) within arm's reach of both individuals. Across the 5 frames, the masks track the camera wearer's limbs shifting from reaching into the left supply caddy (0.6–0.8 m away) in frames 1–2 to moving upward and inward in frames 4–5 to overlap with the other person's hand resting atop the lamp (0.3–0.4 m away), while the lamp becomes increasingly occluded by their converging hands. While the map helps isolate the rounded boundary of the nail lamp in frames 1 and 3 and separates the two people's limb regions in frames 1, 4, and 5, it fails to segment smaller objects within arm's reach such as the supply caddy on the left and the corded controller on the lap. Furthermore, the segmentation map is highly unreliable in class labelling and mask consistency: it misclassifies the nail lamp as a 'banana' in frames 1 and 3, mislabels the upper-left chair edge as a 'laptop' in frame 2, merges both people into a single 'person' mask in frames 2 and 3, and leaves large unsegmented black gaps across the towel-draped lap and background chair.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, isolating hand and body configurations within the 0.3–0.7 m workspace in front of and below the downward-looking camera wearer while omitting all background objects and cropped upper torsos. In frame 1 and frame 3, a single small magenta hand skeleton appears on the lower left (about 0.6–0.7 m away) where the camera wearer's left hand reaches into the supply tray, while in frame 3 a larger magenta hand skeleton also appears at the top centre (0.3–0.4 m away) showing the other person's right hand resting flat with fingers splayed downward toward the camera wearer. In frame 4, two magenta hand skeletons appear close together near the centre (within 0.1 m of each other and 0.3–0.4 m from the camera) as the camera wearer's left hand approaches the other person's downward-pointing hand from the lower left, and in frame 5, magenta and yellow skeletal lines overlap at the centre-right as the camera wearer's two hands clasp and partially occlude the other person's fingers. Compared to RGB, the pose map explicitly reveals finger joint articulation, orientation, and inter-hand proximity during the hand-to-hand interaction in frames 3–5, confirming that neither person's head or gaze is within the field of view. However, the map is unreliable in completeness and anatomical attribution, completely missing all hands in frame 2 and the camera wearer's right hand in frames 1, 3, and 4, while hallucinating a distorted yellow torso and limb skeleton across the interacting hands and raised leg rest in frame 5.
